results.title: MBA: Efficient Hardware Accelerator for MXFP4 Quantization via Learnable Block-Wise Affine Transformation
results.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance across a wide range of natural language processing tasks; however, their rapidly growing model sizes pose critical challenges for energy-efficient inference, increasing the demand for low-bit quantization. Although transformation-based methods have shown superior performance in conventional low-bit formats, their efficacy degrades substantially under the MXFP4 format. This degradation arises because these transformations spread outliers across MX block boundaries, inadvertently introducing new outliers within individual blocks. Furthermore, applying these transformations to activations at runtime requires implementing high-precision arithmetic units that incur significant hardware design overhead in terms of area and power. To address these challenges, we propose MBA, a software-hardware co-design framework that enables hardware-efficient and accurate affine transformation-based MXFP4 quantization. MBA learns affine transformation matrices constrained to a block-diagonal structure aligned with the MX block size, and reduces both the number of parameters and computational complexity while maintaining high accuracy. We also implement a dedicated hardware accelerator featuring dual-mode processing elements (PEs) that efficiently support both BF16 and MXFP4 computations. Hardware evaluations on linear-layer matrix multiplication, including the online affine transformation, demonstrate that MBA achieves $2.66\times $ higher TOPS/W and $1.9\times $ higher TOPS/mm2 than the state-of-the-art MX accelerator. Additionally, in the LLaMA3-8B model, our method achieved an average of 65.69% on reasoning tasks, outperforming LATMiX by 2.72%p and demonstrating better performance compared to existing methods across various LLaMA models.

results.title: PrivSeek: Lightweight and Private Inference for Distilled DeepSeek-Qwen via Secret Sharing
results.venue: International Conference on Networking and Network Applications
results.abstract: The open-source large models (LLMs) developed by DeepSeek have demonstrated substantial utility in various applications. However, such LLMs inference services usually require users to upload their private data to backend servers for computation, giving rise to severe risks of data security leakage. Cryptographic techniques such as secure multi-party computation (MPC) and homomorphic encryption provide feasible solutions to the above problems. However, the existing schemes do not securely and efficiently support Grouped Query Attention (GQA) mechanism, SiLU activation layer, etc., thus making it difficult to achieve secure and efficient inference for DeepSeek models. Therefore, we propose PrivSeek, a lightweight and private inference for distilled DeepSeek-Qwen via secret sharing. Firstly, we construct a secure and efficient improved causal self-attention mask mechanism based on secret sharing, and adopt a two-stage calculation method of lower triangle mask and dynamic row normalization to overcome the limitations of arithmetic logic in ciphertext environment while ensuring controllable complexity. Secondly, we construct a secure and efficient SiLU protocol by combining the look-up table(LUT) mechanism and blinding technology, which effectively reduces the nonlinear computational complexity and realizes the lightweight design of secure computing protocol. Experimental results show that PrivSeek achieves 22.52 seconds per token with only $1.2 \%$ deviation from the maximum accuracy of plaintext benchmarks on mainstream datasets.
